bug_description.original: The gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse function does not set variables to null after deinitialization, which allows the variables to be deinitialized twice during cleanup.
bug_description.normalized: The gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse function does not set variables to null after deinitialization, which allows the variables to be deinitialized twice during cleanup.

source.description: The PKCS#12 parser extracts attacker-controlled bag data into the local data datum used to import a CRL.

sink.description: The second deinitialization reads crl->crl from an already freed CRL object.

root_cause.description: On CRL import failure, the function deinitializes *crl but leaves the caller-visible pointer non-null, so cleanup later deinitializes the same object again.

taint_source.description: The harness passes the fuzzer byte buffer to gnutls_pkcs12_import, creating the PKCS#12 object consumed by project parser code; the harness itself is an unscored boundary.

tainted_value_origin.description: First concrete vulnerability-relevant parsed value: DER data for the current PKCS#12 bag element, later interpreted as a CRL.

root_cause_analysis.summary: Attacker-controlled PKCS#12 data reaches gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse as bag data. When a CRL bag is encountered, the parser allocates *crl and tries to import the attacker-controlled CRL DER. On import failure, the vulnerable error path calls gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl) but leaves *crl non-NULL. The common cleanup block later checks crl != NULL && *crl != NULL, sees the stale pointer, and calls gnutls_x509_crl_deinit a second time. The second deinit dereferences the freed CRL object in crl.c, producing the ASan heap-use-after-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch sets *crl = NULL immediately after the first deinit on the CRL import-failure path. The cleanup block therefore does not call gnutls_x509_crl_deinit on the freed object, and the same PoC no longer triggers the ASan crash in the fixed build.
